access_links.label: FEMA USA Structures page (description, access, use cases)

description: USA Structures is a national dataset of building footprints for every structure larger than 450 square feet in all U.S. states and territories, with attributes for occupancy class under FEMA's Building Occupancy Classification standard, address, height, area, building code, estimated population and a unique identifier. It is built by FEMA's Response Geospatial Office with Oak Ridge National Laboratory, which extract outlines from high-resolution satellite imagery with convolutional and later transformer models on high-performance computers, then attribute them from more than 57 authoritative layers and residence-type models; the USGS National Map Corps verifies occupancy classes. It serves disaster preparedness, response, recovery and mitigation. Launched in 2021, it is updated annually in batches of states; the hosted layer held 135,321,228 features on 26 September 2026 and its data were last edited on 23 September 2025. Access: an ArcGIS Online feature layer in the Living Atlas and File Geodatabase downloads by state. Licence: the page calls it open access geospatial data without naming a licence; it is free. Caveats: footprints and attributes are modelled, population is an estimate with a confidence interval, and structures under 450 square feet are excluded. Simulation uses are exposure for hazard and consequence analysis, emergency response and resilience planning. Related records: USACE National Structure Inventory (point inventory for consequence models), Microsoft US Building Footprints.
